拉塞尔赢得阿塞拜疆大奖赛冠军，将其梅赛德斯队友安东内利的积分领先优势缩小到66分，赛季还剩八轮；从周五上午起，可在天空体育上观看F1重返马来西亚的直播，雪邦将承办巴林大奖赛
梅赛德斯车手安东内利表示阿塞拜疆大奖赛是“那种你只能对第五名感到满意的日子”，但他补充说在马来西亚大奖赛上他会“回到我的水平”
世界冠军领跑者安东内利表示，在阿塞拜疆被梅赛德斯队友拉塞尔压制后，他将在本周末的巴林大奖赛上对拉塞尔“重新确立排位”
安东内利在此前连续五场大奖赛中都跑赢了拉塞尔，但在巴库只能名列第五，因为这位英国车手打出了本赛季最好的一个周末，从杆位出发夺得了冠军。这一结果使安东内利对梅赛德斯队友的领先优势缩小到66分，赛季还剩下八轮比赛。
尽管安东内利挽回了一些积分，但他的表现在三连赛的第二站之前仍有很大的提升空间，由于中东冲突持续，改期后的巴林大奖赛将在马来西亚举行。

在被问到随着法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿落后超过100分、拉塞尔是否已成为他唯一的争冠对手时，安东内利说："他一直就是我的对手。"
"但我会确保下周重新确立秩序，确保自己回到往常的水准，因为这个周末我开得就像我奶奶一样，所以那不是平时的基米。"
2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛的精彩集锦。
"幸运的是我们马上又有一场比赛，我非常期待它。"
这位20岁的意大利车手度过了一个混乱的周末，先是由于技术问题错过了练习赛的大量赛道时间，随后又在排位赛第一节撞车，导致自己只能从发车区第16位起步。
安东内利补充道："第一次自由练习我只跑了三圈，然后错过了第二次自由练习的一半。到了第三次自由练习，我才开始找回节奏。"
“然后在排位赛里，第一节排位赛（Q1）的那一圈其实还行。但我犯了一个错误，于是再次陷入了恶性循环。
基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛期间撞上护墙。
“到了正赛，我没有信心，整个比赛我只能以八成的状态去驾驶。
“说实话，我在心理上也没法百分之百地推进，因为我已经没有了之前几个周末的那种信心，但在雪邦会好得多。”
'很高兴看到战斗在马来西亚重新打响'
拉塞尔在赛季揭幕战澳大利亚大奖赛中夺冠，进一步印证了他季前作为头号夺冠热门的地位，但随后安东内利连续五场比赛夺得了自己职业生涯的前五场胜利，令他大受震撼。
这位意大利车手目前仍然掌控着争冠形势，而且几乎在每一条赛道上，他的正赛节奏似乎都优于拉塞尔。
阿塞拜疆大奖赛迎来了戏剧性的结局：瓦尔特利·博塔斯在最后一圈撞车，而乔治·拉塞尔以仅十分之一秒的优势击败马克斯·维斯塔潘夺得冠军。
这一局面最终在巴库发生了改变，拉塞尔延续了稳定的状态，在整个周末的每一个阶段都比安东内利更快。
梅赛德斯副领队布拉德利·洛德坚称，拉塞尔的出色表现不会对安东内利造成心理打击。
"我真的不觉得这会有什么影响，"洛德说，他在车队领队托托·沃尔夫缺席的情况下于巴库面对媒体。
"我认为车手们会给自己设定很高的标准，他们希望达到这些标准。"
克雷格·斯莱特在阿塞拜疆大奖赛后给出了他的评价，在这场比赛中，拉塞尔险胜维斯塔潘夺得冠军。
“这支车队最大的财富和优势之一，就是我们拥有两名能够在最前方战斗的车手，他们能为赛车拿下杆位，交出毫无瑕疵的分站冠军，这也是车队实力的一部分。
“基米把这件事抛在了脑后，在正赛中干得很出色。乔治在领跑时也做了一份令人难以置信的工作，很期待看到他们在马来西亚展开较量。”

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli vows to 're-establish the order' over George Russell at Bahrain GP in Malaysia after losing out in Azerbaijan

George Russell won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix to reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points with eight rounds remaining; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday morning F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli says that the Azerbaijan GP was 'one of those days you have to be happy with P5' but adds that he will be 'back at my level' at the Malaysian Grand Prix.

World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan.

Antonelli had finished ahead of Russell in five successive Grands Prix but could only manage fifth in Baku, as the Brit produced his best weekend of the season to claim victory from pole position. The result cut Antonelli's lead over his Mercedes team-mate to 66 points with eight rounds remaining.

Although he salvaged some points, Antonelli's performance left plenty of room for improvement ahead of the second leg of the triple-header, with Malaysia set to host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Asked whether Russell is now his only title rival after Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton dropped more than 100 points back, Antonelli said: "He's always been my rival.

"But I'll make sure next week I re-establish the order and just make sure that I will be at back at my usual level because this weekend I was driving more like my grandma, so it wasn't the usual Kimi.
Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
"Luckily we have another race coming up, and I'm really looking forward to it."

The 20-year-old Italian endured a scrappy weekend, missing a major chunk of track time in practice because of a technical issue before crashing in the first part of qualifying to leave himself starting from 16th on the grid.
"FP1 I did three laps and then missed the half of FP2," Antonelli added. "In FP3, I was getting to the rhythm.
"And then in qualifying, that Q1 one lap was actually okay. But I did a mistake, and then again you re-enter in the bad loop.
Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP.
"Then in the race, I didn't have the confidence, and I just at drove 80 per cent the whole time.
"Realistically, I wasn't there mentally to be able to push 100 per cent as well because I just didn't have the confidence that I had previous weekends, but it will be much better in Sepang."
'Exciting to see battle resume in Malaysia'

Russell underlined his pre-season status as the clear title favourite by winning the season opener in Australia, only to be stunned as Antonelli then claimed the first five victories of his career in successive races.
The Italian remains in control of the title race and has also appeared to hold a race-pace advantage over Russell at almost every circuit.
The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell just beat Max Verstappen to victory by one tenth of a second.
That finally changed in Baku, where Russell backed up a solid run of form by being faster than Antonelli at every stage of the weekend.
Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord insists the strength of Russell's performance won't amount to a psychological blow for Antonelli.
"I don't really think it makes a difference," said Lord, who address the media in Baku in the absence of team boss Toto Wolff.
"I think the drivers, they're setting themselves their own high standards, and they want to perform to those.
Craig Slater gives his verdict after the Azerbaijan GP, where George Russell pipped Max Verstappen to victory.

"One of the great assets and the great strengths of this team is we've got two drivers who are capable of fighting at the very front, putting the car on pole, delivering flawless race wins, and that's part of the strength of the team.
"Kimi put it behind him and did a great job in the race. George did an incredible job out front, and it'll be exciting to see them going at it in Malaysia."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
